deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a heavily corrected German prose draft, in ink and pencil, for the closing or framing remarks of Riemann's 1859/60 work on plane air waves of finite amplitude, 'Ueber die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite'. It probably belongs to the paper itself or to his Selbstanzeige in the Göttinger Nachrichten. The surrounding folios are letter drafts to Dedekind and to Wilhelm Weber about Regnault's measured speed of sound (about 332 m/s), which places the page in the same period and context.

The argument, as far as it can be read, runs as follows:
- Several opening attempts are struck out: 'Es scheint ...', 'Dagegen ... liefert die Sache ...', and 'Es scheint auch, dass für die Gesetze der Fortpflanzung ... zu den genauen Differentialgleichungen'.
- The surviving sense is that the laws following from the exact (nonlinear) differential equations of gas motion cannot be applied to the explanation of acoustic phenomena.
- The reason given is that the conditions concerning the origin and propagation of sound are not yet established precisely enough, or are too simple, for these laws to be submitted to experimental test.
- Such applications would therefore lead only to mere conjectures ('als zu bloßen Vermuthungen führen zu können').
- By contrast, the laws flowing from the exact differential equations might perhaps give meteorology some foothold ('vielleicht der Meteorologie einigen Anhalt geben').
- A final struck-out line probably begins a remark about neglected internal friction of the fluid ('Wenn die ... Flüssigkeitsreibung'?).

There is no derivation to restate in modern notation. In context, the 'exact differential equations' are the 1D isentropic Euler equations. For these, Riemann introduced the Riemann invariants r, s = (1/2)(F(rho) ± u), with F(rho) = ∫ sqrt(phi'(rho))/rho drho. He also derived shock ('Verdichtungsstoß') formation. None of this is written on this page.

The page belongs to the methodological and applied framing: Riemann disclaiming direct acoustic testability and suggesting a possible meteorological relevance.
errors: No mathematical steps to check. Physically, the remark matches Riemann's published caveat that his finite-amplitude results are not readily testable acoustically. The suggestion of meteorological relevance is speculative, but it is not an error.

results.what: Remark that the laws derived from the exact nonlinear gas-dynamic equations cannot yet be tested against acoustic experiment and might instead be of use to meteorology
results.modern_name: Framing/application remarks on finite-amplitude (nonlinear) acoustics and shock formation in 1D isentropic gas dynamics
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1860 (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 8) and his Selbstanzeige in the Göttinger Nachrichten 1859

deep.surprise_reason: This is a prose draft of known remarks accompanying Riemann's published 1860 paper on air waves of finite amplitude. It contains no new mathematics, only drafting variants of an application caveat.

checkable.sympy: rho, u = symbols('rho u', positive=True); c = Function('c')(rho); r = (Integral(c/rho, rho) + u)/2; s = (Integral(c/rho, rho) - u)/2
checkable.asserts: Context only, not on this page: these are Riemann's invariants for 1D isentropic flow with sound speed c(rho)=sqrt(p'(rho)). They are constant along dx/dt = u ± c.

transcription_corrections: The line given as 'Immer verdient kein Interesse mehr, als zu bloßen Vermuthungen führen zu können' more likely begins 'Sie würden demnach kein[?] ... haben, als zu bloßen Vermuthungen führen zu können'. 'Immer verdient' appears to be a misreading.
The interlinear '{+zu knüpfen[?]+}' above 'um sie an ...' is more plausibly 'zugänglich': 'um sie der Prüfung zugänglich [zu machen]'.

The line read as 'über Fortpflanzung sind schon zu ...' appears to read 'über Entstehung[?] des Schalls ... zu einfach'. The topic is the origin and propagation of sound, with the insertion 'nicht genau genug festgestellt'.
The superscript read as '{+die Integration[?]+}' is uncertain from the image. It may instead be 'die Störungen[?]' or similar.
'Die Methode[?]' at the start of the main paragraph may be 'Die Resultate[?]'; uncertain.
The struck-out final line 'Wenn die natürliche[?] Flüssigkeit[?] ...' may read '... Flüssigkeitsreibung ...' (fluid friction); uncertain.
The word read as 'Meteorologie' near the bottom is confirmed by the image: 'vielleicht der Meteorologie einigen Anhalt geben'.
